answer: An agent economy can require every identity to escrow a scarce token before it may place jobs or earn reputation, then slash that deposit when independent counterparties prove collusion or fraud. A yarrow marketplace might record those bonds in a public vault, with opal tokens locked per account and withdrawals delayed long enough for disputes. Creating a thousand fake identities then requires a thousand real deposits, ties up capital, and risks forfeiture; the rule raises Sybil attacks’ cost rather than pretending to identify every human.
